B. Every call after that: the steady state, until the token Foundry holds expires (60-90 minutes)
Wall 1: validate-jwt (audience = the wall API app, tenant, tid), then
abw-deny (kill switch, azp allow-list, scope, role) and 120 calls per
Wall 2: verify T2 again (RS256 signature via JWKS, audience, v2.0

the project (falcon) must be in the token's roles.

Authentication flow: who proves what, with which token
First call: one-time consent. Every call after: user token, managed identity, OBO, data
Agents Behind the Wall - diagram 04 of 13 - generated by docs/diagrams/build_diagrams.py
persona in a browser, or the
- Three tokens meet at the MCP server: T2 comes in from the user, T3 proves the server's
own identity, and T4 goes out to the data as the user.
- No MCP server holds a client secret: T3 is a managed identity token, trusted through a
federated credential. The only OAuth client secret, abw-agent-client's, sits in the five
Foundry OAuth connections and the git-ignored .secrets folder.
- A role change reaches the gateway with the next token you request (up to about 30 s; one
removal lagged longer), but the agent keeps the T2 Foundry already holds until it expires.
Tokens in this diagram (T1-T4 mean the same in diagrams 01, 03, 07, 11 and 13; the document also writes T2a, T2b and T4a-c)
User token for Foundry, sent with
oid, tid, upn or preferred_username; a delegated token, not app-only
User token for one MCP API; Foundry
mints it after the consent and holds it
scp Tools.Read (Tools.Execute on actions); roles = the user's app roles;
Managed identity token of the MCP
sub = the UAMI principal; iss = the tenant's v2.0 endpoint
On-behalf-of token for one data plane
oid = the user; azp = the MCP API app; scp user_impersonation
